review.translation: [So|0] [the heavens|1] [and the earth|2] [and all|3] [their host|4] [were completed|0].

analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with the compound subject הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ וְכָל־צְבָאָם, “the heavens and the earth and all their host.” The Pual presents them as having been brought to completion.
analysis.morphology: Pual wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: The verb וַיְכֻלּוּ (“were completed”) applies to הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ (“the heavens and the earth”). The phrase וְכָל־צְבָאָם (“and all their host”) reinforces the pair’s reference to the whole of creation.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ pairs the heavens and the earth as the two parts of the completed creation. צְבָאָם (“their host”) refers back to both.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus definite article הָ plus common noun אָרֶץ, singular absolute, common gender.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל צְבָאָם, “and all their host,” כָל quantifies the collective noun צְבָאָם. The host of the heavens and the earth is included in its entirety.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וְ.

analysis.evidence: The suffix in צְבָאָם refers back to הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ, “the heavens and the earth.” The singular noun gathers their contents into one host, and כָל makes the reference comprehensive: “all their host.”
analysis.morphology: Common-gender singular noun in the construct state with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix ־ָם.
analysis.sense: host, collectively the creatures and things that fill heaven and earth
